title: Acoustic and perceptual differences between standard and accented speech and their voice clones
abstract: arXiv:2604.01562v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Voice cloning is often evaluated in terms of overall quality, but less is known about accent preservation and its perceptual consequences. We compare standard and heavily accented Mandarin speech and their voice clones using a combined computational and perceptual design. Embedding-based analyses showed larger original-clone distances for accented speakers in several speaker-discriminative embedding spaces, but this difference disappeared after adjusting for each speaker's within-original baseline variability. In the perception study, clones are rated as more similar to their originals for standard than for accented speakers, and intelligibility increases from original to clone, with a larger gain for accented speech. translated_title: 标准语音与口音语音及其语音克隆之间的声学与感知差异
translated_abstract: 语音克隆通常以整体质量来评估，但对其口音保留程度及其感知后果的了解却较少。我们采用计算与感知相结合的设计，比较了标准普通话与重口音普通话语音及其对应的语音克隆。基于嵌入的分析显示，在多个说话人判别嵌入空间中，口音说话人的原始语音与克隆语音之间的距离更大，但在对每个说话人原始语音内部的基线变异性进行调整后，这一差异消失了。在感知研究中，标准说话人的克隆语音被评为与其原始语音更相似，而从原始语音到克隆语音，可懂度有所提升，且口音语音的增益更大。这些结果表明，即使在经过基线调整的说话人嵌入距离中观察不到口音变异的影响，它仍能影响语音克隆中感知到的身份匹配度和可懂度，这也促使人们……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究发现，口音变异虽不体现在经基线调整的说话人嵌入距离中，却会显著影响语音克隆的感知身份匹配度和可懂度，且口音语音克隆后的可懂度提升幅度更大。
en_tdlr: The study shows that accent variation shapes perceived identity match and intelligibility in voice cloning—even when unobservable in baseline-adjusted speaker-embedding distance—with accented speech gaining more intelligibility after cloning.
